areasReviewed: Denial of service and hidden data channels

findings.evidence: PORT-EVIDENCE-OMITTED.txt explicitly states that upstream sources are excluded. The manifest declares a specific VS Code revision and MIT-licensed port.
findings.impact: The claimed upstream relationship, palette derivation and license provenance cannot be independently established.
findings.title: Declared upstream evidence omitted

findings.evidence: Documentation claims real Windows screenshots and Chromium fixture results, but neither image contents nor fixture source/results are supplied. adaptation.md also says screenshots are pending, contradicting the README.
findings.impact: Application coverage and screenshot authenticity remain unverified; documentation contains stale or inconsistent validation claims.
findings.title: Screenshot and fixture claims lack supporting artifacts

findings.evidence: Both modes contain 21 literal hex or rgba color values. No executable code, CSS payload, dependencies or build scripts appear in the supplied bundle.
findings.impact: Under the stated host allowlist, the supplied theme provides no apparent execution, graph modification, protocol abuse or data-exfiltration mechanism.
findings.title: Theme payload has limited execution risk

aiReview.summary: The manifest contains only inert literal colors and shows no executable payload. Quarantine is required because upstream provenance and several validation claims cannot be verified from the supplied bundle.

manualApproval.note: Inert colour theme; upstream port evidence (microsoft/vscode) is too large to include, so it was omitted by design (D-20261027-TH).
